section.p: Both versions use the same Admin Panel, include the access controller, can act as a Thread Border Router and mesh router, and need power, compatible lock hardware and wiring. What differs is the connection:
Ask us which version suits your region. The connection is chosen door by door.

section.h2: Every reader is a Thread router and Border Router

div.p: Each SmartphoneKey reader can act as a Thread Border Router and as a router in the Thread mesh. Neither role needs a separate firmware version, so the readers on a site can form one mesh and connect it to your IP network.
A suitable wireless design can reduce communication cabling between readers: readers on the Thread mesh can reach the internet through a reader that has an LTE or Wi-Fi connection.

Mesh coverage and the route to the internet still depend on placement, power and the building. How many readers share one connection, and what happens if it drops, depend on the installation; automatic failover is not implied. Matter controller functions are confirmed for each project.
Coverage depends on the building, placement and radio conditions. We help plan the network for your site.

div.h3: How do the LTE and Wi-Fi readers differ?
div.p: They connect differently. The LTE reader uses a cellular network and needs a SIM and service; the Wi-Fi reader uses the site's Wi-Fi and needs reliable coverage and network settings. Check the connection at each door position.

div.h3: Can one reader provide connectivity for other readers?
div.p: Yes. Every reader can act as a Thread router and as a Border Router, so readers can share a Thread mesh and reach the internet through a reader that has a connection. How many readers share that connection, and what happens if it drops, depend on the installation; we plan the topology with you. Automatic failover is not implied.

div.h3: How far apart can readers be installed?
div.p: Coverage depends on the building, obstacles, placement and hardware configuration. Plan and check coverage on site; no single distance fits every installation.

div.h3: Can I keep existing locks or cameras?
div.p: Check the exact lock hardware, its electrical interface and the camera models first. Send us the model details before you plan to reuse an existing installation.

t.t: What works depends on the reader configuration, the card product, the phone and the capabilities each device reports. The tables list what is documented; ask us to confirm anything else for your project.

div.p: Supported SmartphoneKey reader configurations also let you program MIFARE Classic and MIFARE DESFire EV3 cards. A family name does not cover every memory size, credential format or card from another supplier. Reading a card, programming it and assigning access are separate operations.
Wallet keys depend on the phone, its operating system and the account configuration. Do not assume a key works the same way on every phone when its battery is low or empty.

Support depends on capabilities. A device may report on/off, contact, temperature, lock, valve or other capabilities; what you can do with it depends on what it reports and what your configuration supports. Specific third-party models are listed only after compatibility testing.

div.p: Supported SmartphoneKey reader configurations can program MIFARE Classic and MIFARE DESFire EV3 cards. Confirm the exact card product, memory size and any existing credential format before ordering.

div.h3: Can I use a third-party card programmer?
div.p: No. Cards are programmed with a SmartphoneKey reader that supports programming; SmartphoneKey does not support third-party card programmers.

div.h3: Does SmartphoneKey work with every Matter device?
div.p: It depends on the device type, the capabilities it reports, its firmware and your configuration. Check the functions your scenario needs rather than assuming every Matter device offers them.
